terms.definition: A pure substance made of two or more different elements chemically bonded together.
terms.function: Forms a new substance whose properties belong to no single element.
terms.whereItIs: The water, carbon dioxide, and salt in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Compounds are water, salt, sugar, and nearly everything you can name.

terms.definition: The force that holds a compound's different elements together.
terms.function: Turns separate elements into one new substance with a fixed ratio.
terms.whereItIs: The bonds inside water and CO₂, and the lattice of salt.
terms.whyItMatters: The bond is what makes a compound a compound, not a mixture.

terms.definition: The new properties a compound has that its elements do not share.
terms.function: Explains why salt is safe even though its elements are dangerous.
terms.whereItIs: Shown on the identity card in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: New identity is the most surprising and important fact about compounds.

terms.definition: The exact, unchanging proportion of elements in a compound.
terms.function: Makes each compound a unique substance — water is always 2H to 1O.
terms.whereItIs: Every compound in the model has its own fixed recipe.
terms.whyItMatters: Fixed ratios are what make compounds identifiable and predictable.
